pt.hero|title: One picture of the situation. An extra sense for every responder.
pt.hero|sub: Watchtower links crews, coordinators and companies on a live map of the world — and watches the sky, the ground and the team around each person, so warnings reach them before the danger does.
pt.problem|lead: After-action reviews of recent disasters keep naming the same failures.
pt.problem|items|0|1: Commanders on different screens, crews on different channels — nobody sees the whole situation.
pt.problem|items|1|1: Regional forecasts generalize; a storm cell over one crew can be invisible in the area forecast.
pt.problem|items|2|1: Personnel accountability still runs on radio roll calls that are slow to notice silence.
pt.features|items|0|2: Satellite, radar, cloud movement, lidar terrain, earthquakes and wildfires on one globe — every layer from a public, citable science source.
pt.features|items|1|1: An extra sense around each person
pt.features|items|1|2: Every five minutes the tower reads the actual radar over each crew member, the next hour of rain, and the next three days of wind, heat, cold and storms at their exact position — then pushes what matters to their phone.
pt.features|items|2|2: Coordinators ask "are you OK?"; everyone answers with one glove-friendly tap and their position. Silence turns amber, then red, and the tower re-alerts automatically.
pt.features|items|3|2: Response protocols as shared checklists the whole team works in real time — drafted by AI, launched from an alert in one tap, debriefed automatically afterwards.
pt.features|items|4|2: Live crew positions, markers everyone can move, team chat with voice dictation — translated into each reader's language. Vehicle mode turns a cab tablet into one glanceable screen.
pt.features|items|5|2: Voice-driven patient records with triage, offline queueing and an AI-composed handover for the receiving hospital.
pt.features|items|6|2: Your day at your position, your team's three-day outlook, and the El Niño / La Niña context for the months ahead.
pt.features|items|7|2: Each organization runs its own private Watchtower; linked companies share their tactical picture during joint operations.
pt.features|items|8|2: Every prediction Watchtower makes is recorded with its variables, frozen, and checked against what really happened — alongside the region's memory of fires, floods and quakes, and a live log of every action in the operation.
pt.features|items|9|2: Drones, cameras and sensors registered in one place with their live status. Video ingest is the next step on the roadmap.
pt.how|title: How it helps — a real example
pt.how|steps|0|1: A violent storm cell builds over a crew. The area forecast still says 0 mm.
pt.how|steps|1|1: The tower reads the radar over each crew member and finds 45 dBZ directly over one of them.
pt.how|steps|2|1: Every phone in the crew buzzes: "Intense cell over your position" — in each person's own language.
pt.how|steps|3|1: The coordinator taps Run protocol: the severe-weather checklist reaches everyone, and a check-in confirms all are sheltered.
pt.how|steps|4|1: An AI debrief records what happened and what to improve — the crew's memory for next time.
pt.science|lead: Watchtower shows its sources so you can check them.
pt.science|sources: NASA GIBS satellites · NOAA GOES & Himawari · RainViewer radar · Open-Meteo & ECMWF forecasts · USGS earthquakes · NASA EONET events · NOAA Climate Prediction Center · NRCan & Esri lidar terrain

pt.tour|steps|0|2: Watchtower is your team's shared picture of the situation. This tour shows the main screens in about three minutes. You can open it again any time from the homepage.
pt.tour|steps|0|3|1: Your team on a tactical map
pt.tour|steps|1|1: Install it and turn on alerts
pt.tour|steps|1|2: On your phone, open Watchtower in the browser and choose "Add to Home Screen" (or "Install app"). Then tap "Enable notifications" in the menu — alerts reach you even when the app is closed.
pt.tour|steps|2|2: Open My settings and pick your language. Screens follow it, and everything your team writes — messages, alerts, notes — is translated for you, with the original one tap away.
pt.tour|steps|2|3|2: My settings → Appearance: light, dark, night vision, sunlight, your colour
pt.tour|steps|3|2: World is the live globe: radar, satellite clouds, wildfires, earthquakes, terrain. Forecasts gives your day and week at your position, your team's outlook and the season ahead.
pt.tour|steps|3|3|1: Layers → Bare earth, then ◎ to see one layer alone
pt.tour|steps|3|3|2: Play the radar and cloud loop
pt.tour|steps|3|3|4: Forecasts → Area history and Track record
pt.tour|steps|4|2: You do not have to watch the sky. Every five minutes the tower checks radar, rain, wind, heat, cold, earthquakes and fires around your position and pushes what matters. Each morning you get a short brief for your day.
pt.tour|steps|4|3|0: Bell icon = everything waiting for you
pt.tour|steps|4|3|1: Red = act now · amber = be aware
pt.tour|steps|5|2: When a coordinator asks for a check-in, a full screen appears: tap I'M OK or NEED HELP. Your position goes with it. If you stay silent, the tower asks again and tells your coordinator.
pt.tour|steps|5|3|1: NEED HELP alerts the whole team
pt.tour|steps|6|2: The tactical map shows your team live, plus markers anyone can drag into place. Comms is the team channel — type or dictate.
pt.tour|steps|6|3|0: Drag a marker from the palette
pt.tour|steps|6|3|1: Tap the mic to dictate a message
pt.tour|steps|6|3|2: In a vehicle: menu → Vehicle mode — one big screen, read aloud
pt.tour|steps|7|2: Record patients by voice: "new patient", "patient 2 triage red". Entries queue offline and sync later. One tap composes a hospital handover.
pt.tour|steps|7|3|3: ✏️ correct or 🗑 remove a note — the original stays in its history
pt.tour|steps|8|2: Protocols are shared checklists for situations like a fire approaching or a storm inbound. Ask the AI assistant anything about the operation — it can also start a protocol or message the team for you.
pt.tour|steps|9|2: The Team tab holds your roster, teams, invitations (QR codes) and check-in board. Settings sets alert ranges and check-in rules for your organization.
pt.tour|steps|9|3|3: Team → Comms quality: every member’s link, live · Tactical map → Signal: coverage history
